D000718.s: The anatomical study of specific regions or parts of organisms, emphasizing the relationship between the various structures (e.g. muscles, nerves, skeletal, cardiovascular, etc.).

D001267.s: Body of water separating North and South America from Africa and Europe.

D001469.s: Injury following pressure changes; includes injury to the eustachian tube, ear drum, lung and stomach.

D001890.s: An encephalomyelitis of horses, sheep and cattle caused by borna disease virus.

D001924.s: A nonspecific term used to describe transient alterations or loss of consciousness following closed head injuries. The duration of unconsciousness generally lasts a few seconds, but may persist for several hours. Concussions may be classified as mild, intermediate, and severe.

D002903.s: The short, metacentric human chromosomes, called group F in the human chromosome classification. This group consists of chromosome pairs 19 and 20.

D003827.s: A complete denture replacing all the natural maxillary teeth and associated maxillary structures. It is completely supported by the oral tissue and underlying maxillary bone.

D004260.s: The removal of dna lesions and/or restoration of intact DNA strands without base pair mismatches, intrastrand or interstrand crosslinks, or discontinuities in the DNA sugar-phosphate backbones.

D004387.s: A fibromatosis of the palmar fascia characterized by thickening and contracture of the fibrous bands on the palmar surfaces of the hand and fingers. It arises most commonly in men between the ages of 30 and 50.

D004530.s: Cytoplasm stored in an egg that contains nutritional reserves for the developing embryo. It is rich in polysaccharides, lipids, and proteins.

D005137.s: A ready-made or custom-made prosthesis of glass or plastic shaped and colored to resemble the anterior portion of a normal eye and used for cosmetic reasons.

D006132.s: The area between the epiphysis and the diaphysis within which bone growth occurs.

D007207.s: A process of differentiation having for its goal the development of the individual personality.

D007896.s: A disease caused by any of a number of species of protozoa in the genus leishmania.

D008369.s: Method of nonverbal communication utilizing hand movements as speech equivalents.

D012223.s: A form of non-allergic rhinitis that is characterized by nasal congestion and posterior pharyngeal drainage.

D012681.s: A group of people who meet in an unstructured setting to learn about themselves, interpersonal relationships, and group processes and about larger social systems.

D012807.s: A republic in western Africa, south of guinea and west of liberia. Its capital is Freetown.

D016375.s: Nucleic acids which hybridize to complementary sequences in other target nucleic acids causing the function of the latter to be affected.

D017835.s: A pyranoquinolone derivative that inhibits activation of inflammatory cells which are associated with asthma, including eosinophils; neutrophils; macrophages; mast cells; monocytes; and platelets.

D018526.s: The loss of water vapor by plants to the atmosphere. It occurs mainly from the leaves through pores (stomata) whose primary function is gas exchange. D019635.s: Surgery performed on the nervous system or its parts.

D020468.s: Work consisting of information presented in graphic form, for example, graphs or diagrams.

D020521.s: A group of pathological conditions characterized by sudden, non-convulsive loss of neurological function due to brain ischemia or intracranial hemorrhages.

D020554.s: An assisted fertilization technique consisting of the microinjection of a single viable sperm into an extracted ovum. D047830.s: United Nations' action to intervene in conflict between the nation of Kuwait and occupying Iraqi forces, occurring from 1990 through 1991.

D058070.s: Diseases that do not exhibit symptoms.
